protocol.timer_start: Start immediately after the participant sees the task card and has a clean working directory.
protocol.timer_stop: Stop only after the observable acceptance condition passes.
protocol.setup: Install and verify the assigned language toolchain before the timed task. Use the same editor and comparable machine for a cohort.
protocol.resources: Official language and standard-library documentation is allowed. Log documentation, hint and assistance events. Run assisted/AI cohorts separately from unassisted cohorts.
protocol.privacy: Use an opaque participant code. Do not record names, email addresses, source code, terminal history or unrelated personal information.
protocol.comparison: Publish sample counts, failures and raw aggregate timing evidence. Do not claim one language is easier or faster from an unbalanced or tiny cohort.

tasks.title: Print a first program
tasks.goal: Create and run a program that prints exactly: Hello, world!
tasks.acceptance: The program exits successfully and stdout contains exactly one line: Hello, world!

tasks.title: Build a small CLI
tasks.goal: Build a command-line program that accepts a name argument and prints: Hello, <name>!
tasks.acceptance: Running the program with Ada as the argument exits successfully and prints exactly: Hello, Ada!

tasks.title: Build a tiny HTTP API
tasks.goal: Start an HTTP server with GET /health returning a JSON object whose ok field is true.
tasks.acceptance: A local HTTP request to /health returns status 200, Content-Type application/json, and parseable JSON with ok=true.

tasks.title: Build a JSON transformation tool
tasks.goal: Read a JSON file containing an array of records and write the count of records whose active field is true.
tasks.acceptance: Given the study fixture with three records, two active, the program exits successfully and prints exactly: 2

tasks.title: Build local database CRUD
tasks.goal: Create a local users store, insert Ada, read Ada, update the name to Ada Lovelace, then delete the record.
tasks.acceptance: The observer can verify create, read, update and delete in one run or documented sequence, with the final lookup returning no Ada record.
